title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
summary: Given a 1-indexed array of integers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two distinct indices such that the elements at these indices add up to a specific target number.
statement: Given a 1-indexed array of integers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two distinct indices such that the elements at these indices add up to a specific target number. Return the indices, each incremented by one, as an integer array of length 2. There is exactly one solution for the given input, and you must not use the same element twice. Your solution should use only constant extra space.
constraints: numbers is sorted nondecreasing and contains 2..30000 integers.
Exactly one distinct pair reaches target; return one-based indices using O(1) extra space.
reference_solution:
def two_sum_sorted_indices(numbers, target):
 left,right=0,len(numbers)-1
 while left<right:
  total=numbers[left]+numbers[right]
  if total==target:return [left+1,right+1]
  if total<target:left+=1
  else:right-=1

hints: The smallest and largest remaining values bound every unexamined pair.
Start pointers at both ends of the sorted array.
If the sum is low, advance left; if high, retreat right; return the one-based positions on equality.
The discarded endpoint cannot participate in a solution after the comparison.
